title: Native event emitter
summary: Subscriptions that start native observation on the first listener and stop on the last.
prompt: Write `createEmitter(native)` where `native` has `startObserving(event)` and `stopObserving(event)`. Return `{ addListener(event, fn), emit(event, payload), listenerCount(event) }`. `addListener` returns `{ remove() }`. Call `startObserving(event)` when an event gets its first listener and `stopObserving(event)` when its last listener is removed. `remove` is idempotent. `emit` calls the listeners registered at the time of the emit, in order, so a listener removed during an emit does not stop the others from running in that emit. The same function added twice is two subscriptions. There is no React Native runtime here, so this is modelled as plain TypeScript.
hints: Store subscriptions in a `Map<string, Array<{ fn }>>` and remove by object identity.
Copy the array before iterating in `emit`.
Track a `removed` flag on each subscription for idempotent removal.
